why: `let v!: T` turns off TypeScript's check that v is assigned before it is read; read first, v is undefined. The translator once gave such a variable an uninterpreted start value of its type (uninit_T), which proved late's `return v` equal to `return v + 0` (undefined against NaN when flag is false). Now (design/opaque-values.md) such a let is an option that starts absent, and a read TypeScript did not check is its payload only after the statement's test; where it is absent the unit's result is an opaque value named by the file's text. late: lane B witnesses, lane A does not prove it against the candidate, and proves the parent against itself (the same file: the reading lifts the refusal, PASS-bounded became PASS-proved). early, assigned first, is proved on a refactor; plain untouched, proved.
